title: Cell volume and geometric parameters determination in living cells using confocal microscopy and 3D reconstruction
protocol: Harvest cells growing in monolayer in T-75 ml cell culture flasks.
Add 5.0 ml of trypsin-EDTA to each plate and incubate at room temperature for 4 min.
Transfer the cell suspension into a 15 ml conical tube using 5.0 ml of RPMI 1640 with 10% FBS and 25 mM HEPES cell culture medium.
Pellet suspended cells in 15 ml conical tubes using a centrifuge for 5 min at 500g.
Re-suspend each cell pellet in 2-3 ml of media and perform cell counts.
Place a coverslip inside culture plates \(6 well-plate) with sterilized tweezers.
Add complete media to culture plates \(2 ml) without dropping media over the coverslips.
Seed cells at an appropriate final density \(50,000 cells/ml but may vary depending on cell type/size).
Shake plates slowly to homogenize cell distribution.
Add 2 ml of fresh RPMI medium with 0.2% FBS in new 6 well plates.
Use three wells for washing with PBS-glucose solution.
Shake to homogenize a mixture of 20 µl AO solution and RPMI medium from three plates.
Place each coverslip containing cells into one of the wells with washing solution for 1 minute.
Transfer coverslips into wells containing staining solution for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Pipette 100 μl of RPMI medium with 0.2% FBS onto a clean slide.
Place coverslips with cells upside-down over the medium on the slide using mounting medium only along the external limits to avoid auto-fluorescence.
Immediately place the mounted slide under the confocal microscope with one drop of immersion oil.
Run the software with the settings indicated for equipment setup.
Search an area of interest including as many individual cells as possible.
Indicate coordinates to create 1 µm depth slices for analysis.
Store images captured from the slices for further processing.
Repeat the process described until a number over 100 cells is reached.
Run the ‘Imaris’ program for processing images.
In the menu ‘File’, select ‘Open’ and click on the first section image to open all section images taken.
Select ‘volume’, then ‘surface’, and click the `blend` button.
Press ‘Ctrl+D’ in the keyboard, a new window will pop up. Select “auto blend” and close this window.
Select ‘surface’ and press the blue bottom of play two times.
Click on the ‘play’ button to open a new window filled with several lines corresponding to different cell volumes.
Move the threshold line up to eliminate objects that correspond to incomplete cells or cut-off cells.
Select tab labeled as ‘pencil’, then click on ‘select’ for selecting all incomplete cells.
Delete those selected incomplete cells.
